findings.text: §16's key rule forbids door-local inputs and then makes the last resort "the dispatched attempt", which is door-local and cannot be reached on any door that reserves (each writes its marker before reserving, so reading 2 always answers)

findings.reason: the omission cannot produce a wrong design, only a first-run crash the implementer meets at the first dispatch test and fixes with a guard, so the plan's mechanism and its done-when are unaffected.
findings.text: the third reading is "the attempt the live pointer records for the run" with no statement of what happens when there is no pointer, and `read_pointer` raises `CrewError` for an unknown run, which is the state of every fresh dispatch at the moment `reserve_launch_attempt` computes its key

response_events.note: The door-local fallback is removed: every reserving door finds a marker or earlier traces on disk before it keys (a dispatch writes its marker first; a resume holds the earlier attempt's trace), so the key is the greatest of the on-disk readings and no door's own dispatched attempt enters it.
§16 now says the pointer reading is absent when the run has no pointer yet, as on every fresh dispatch at the moment it keys, and never raises.
